ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Two sound sources $\mathrm{S}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{2}$, vibrating at a constant and synchronous frequency, are placed 12 m apart. An observer moves along the line connecting $\mathrm{S}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{2}$ and hears fluctuations in the volume, with one of the positions of minimum volume being 5 m away from $\mathrm{S}_{1}$. The speed of sound is $340\mathrm{m/s}$.

1. Find the minimum frequency of the sound source vibration.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Two sound sources $\mathrm{S}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{2}$, vibrating at a constant and synchronous frequency, are placed 12 m apart. An observer moves along the line connecting $\mathrm{S}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{2}$ and hears fluctuations in the volume, with one of the positions of minimum volume being 5 m away from $\mathrm{S}_{1}$. The speed of sound is $340\mathrm{m/s}$. Find the minimum frequency of the sound source vibration.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Read the given text: the distance between the two synchronous sound sources is S1S2 = 12 m. The observer is on the line between them, at a position 5 m from S1 where the volume is minimum. Therefore the observer’s distance from S2 is 12 - 5 = 7 m. The path difference of the two sounds at that point is |7 - 5| = 2 m. For destructive interference from synchronous sources, the path difference satisfies Δ = (n + 1/2)λ, where n = 0, 1, 2, .... Thus 2 = (n + 1/2)λ. To get the minimum frequency f = v/λ, the wavelength must be as large as possible, so choose n = 0. Then 2 = λ/2, so λ = 4 m. With sound speed v = 340 m/s, f = v/λ = 340/4 = 85 Hz.
